'''Erwin Lutwak''' (born 9 February 1946, [[Chernivtsi]], now [[Ukraine]]), is a [[mathematician]]. Lutwak is [[professor emeritus]] at the [[Courant Institute|Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]] in [[New York City]].  His main research interests are [[convex geometry]] and its connections with [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]] and [[information theory]].

==Biography==
He spent the earliest years of his childhood in the Soviet Union, Romania, Israel, Italy, and Venezuela before he settled in Brooklyn when he was ten. He graduated from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn, now [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in 1968, a [[Master of Science|M.S.]] in 1972 and with a [[Ph.D.]] in 1974.  Before he became professor at the [[Courant Institute]] at [[NYU]], he was a professor at [[New York University Tandon School of Engineering]]. His first position in 1975 was at the Polytechnic Institute of New York (which was created as a result of the merger of the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn and the NYU School of Engineering).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://engineering.nyu.edu/news/2014/11/20/professor-mathematics-erwin-lutwak-might-be-feted-worlds-capitals-brooklyn-remains-h|title=Professor of Mathematics Erwin Lutwak Might Be Feted in the World's Capitals but Brooklyn Remains Home|website=Engineering.nyu.edu|accessdate=26 November 2017}}</ref>

He is a member of the editorial boards of the [[Advances in Mathematics]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/advances-in-mathematics/editorial-board
|title=Advances in Mathematics - Editorial Board|accessdate=15 January 2019}}</ref>
the [[Canadian Journal of Mathematics]],<ref name=CJM>{{cite web|url=https://cms.math.ca/Docs/commlist.html/#cjmcmb-board|title=CJM/CMB Editorial Board|accessdate=15 January 2019|archive-date=15 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190115234538/https://cms.math.ca/Docs/commlist.html/#cjmcmb-board|url-status=dead}}</ref> the [[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]],<ref name=CJM /> and the [[Cambridge University Press]] Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/series/encyclopedia-of-mathematics-and-its-applications/14161A9F36D6D0C9A650A4F86F74162D
|title=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications|accessdate=15 January 2019}}</ref>
He is an Honorary Editor at Advanced Nonlinear Studies (De Gruyter).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.degruyter.com/journal/key/ans/html#editorial|title=Advanced Nonlinear Studies - Editorial Board|accessdate=2023-09-12}}</ref>

==Work==
Erwin Lutwak is known for his Dual Brunn Minkowski Theory,<ref>{{citation|first=Erwin|last=Lutwak|title= Dual mixed volumes |journal=[[Pacific Journal of Mathematics]]|volume=58|issue=2|year=1975|pages=531–538|doi=10.2140/pjm.1975.58.531|doi-access=free}}</ref> 
his notion of [[intersection body]] and his contribution to the solution of the [[Busemann–Petty problem]],<ref>{{citation|first=Erwin|last=Lutwak|title= Intersection bodies and dual mixed volumes |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|volume=71|issue=2|year=1988|pages=232–261|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(88)90077-1|doi-access=}}.</ref> for proving the long-conjectured upper-semicontinuity of affine surface area,<ref>{{citation|first=Erwin|last=Lutwak|title= Extended affine surface area |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|volume=85|issue=1|year=1991|pages=39–68|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(91)90049-D|doi-access=free}}.</ref> his contributions to the L<sub>p</sub> Brunn Minkowski Theory and, in particular, his L<sub>p</sub> [[Minkowski problem]]<ref>{{citation|first=Erwin|last=Lutwak|title= The Brunn-Minkowski-Firey theory. I. Mixed volumes and the Minkowski problem.  |journal=[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]|volume=38|year=1993|pages=131–150|doi=10.4310/jdg/1214454097|doi-access=free}}.</ref> and its solution in important cases.<ref>{{citation|first1= Karoly| last1= Böröczky| first2=Erwin|last2=Lutwak|first3=Deane| last3= Yang| first4= Gaoyong | last4=Zhang|title=The logarithmic Minkowski problem.  |journal=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=26| issue= 3|year=2013|pages=831–852| doi= 10.1090/S0894-0347-2012-00741-3| url= http://real.mtak.hu/10063/1/carlos2.pdf}}.</ref>

==Honors==
* Lutwak became an Inaugural Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=American Mathematical Society|website=Ams.org|accessdate=26 November 2017|archive-date=25 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref> in 2012.
* He received an [[honorary doctorate]] of the [[TU Wien]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tuwien.ac.at/wir_ueber_uns/zahlen_und_fakten/akademische_wuerdentraeger_innen/|title=Technische Universität Wien : Akademische Würdenträger_innen|website=Tuwien.ac.at|accessdate=26 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221150413/http://www.tuwien.ac.at/wir_ueber_uns/zahlen_und_fakten/akademische_wuerdentraeger_innen/|archive-date=21 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Dr. Lutwak is married to Nancy Lutwak, M.D.. They have one daughter, Hope Lutwak, who graduated with a Bachelor of Science in 2018 from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The family resides in Manhattan.
